key_insight: Human–machine interactions across the entire AI lifecycle determine whether humans retain meaningful control and accountability in military systems; governance must address socio-technical processes, not only isolated technical fixes.
problem_solved: Clarifies how design, deployment and operational practices shift decision authority and blur accountability in military AI, and identifies where interventions are needed to restore meaningful human oversight.
method: Conceptual analysis of human–machine interaction (HMI) across AI lifecycle stages (design, testing, deployment, use, after-action).
Mapping of points where control, information, and responsibility transfer from humans to machines, drawing on policy and empirical literature.
Synthesis of governance and design recommendations that link technical practice to legal, ethical and organizational accountability mechanisms.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper reframes responsibility as a lifecycle design requirement: integrate human-centered controls, transparency and auditability into every stage to preserve oversight and enable accountable use in military contexts.
visual_elements: AI lifecycle diagram annotated with HMI touchpoints where control and accountability shift (design → deployment → use → after-action).
Decision-flow overlay showing degrees of human authority vs automated autonomy at key stages.
Governance checklist/roadmap graphic linking technical measures (e.g., explainability, logging) to policy outcomes (e.g., accountability, legal compliance).
Stakeholder map showing roles (developers, commanders, operators, regulators) and lines of responsibility and information flow.
paper_title: Re-thinking human–machine interaction and the governance of AI in the military domain
